analysis:
Scope: docs/architecture/inference.md only (documentation). The visible changed head range 404-413 (units 8 and 9 cover lines 1-798) documents that Nemotron Super eviction and pre-accept now call releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad, which returns retained free KV segments and drops the MLX buffer cache once. Segments still parked after the release never justify an eviction. The later added range at head lines 1053-1073 (parked free 64 MiB segments up to min(2 GiB, grant/8), outside grant and ledger charge, reinstalled for the same size class) falls outside the supplied text. Only the patch excerpt shows it, and that excerpt is truncated.

Security relevance: the retained-free-KV-segment design touches T-028 (residual inference data in GPU memory after a request completes) and cross-tenant exposure, because parked segments are reused across requests. The docs state new segments wrap zero-fil..., but the excerpt is cut off, so I cannot confirm that reused parked segments are zeroed or that no tenant data persists. The docs also say parked segments sit outside the ledger charge, which affects memory-budget accounting and availability (T-029/DoS class). Because this is a doc-only change and the implementation was not supplied, no finding is raised. The next pass should verify in the source (paged KV backend, segment parking and reinstall) that reused segments cannot expose a prior request's KV contents, that the 2 GiB parked bound is enforced, and that the 'outside ledger' memory cannot cause admission over-commit.

Prefix-cache text in the supplied range (cache-scope partitioning, off without a scope) is consistent with T-041 and introduces no change to its posture. No threat-model assumptions are invalidated by the visible lines.
